context_snapshot.challenge: Cross-functional decisions and ownership are lost between meetings and handoffs.
context_snapshot.desired_outcome: Create a reliable, reviewable path from discussion to confirmed decisions and owned follow-ups.
context_snapshot.work_system_boundary: Meeting notes, decision confirmation, handoff acceptance, and follow-up review across the cross-functional team.
decisions: what counts as a confirmed decision
facts: The department lead retains final decision accountability
The first test cannot write to production systems
assumptions: Lost follow-ups are partly caused by unclear confirmation and handoff practices
unknowns: Which meeting types create the highest rework

candidate_use_cases.title: Human-approved decision and action ledger
candidate_use_cases.workflow_change: AI drafts separate proposed decisions, confirmed decisions, actions, and open questions; owners approve entries before they enter a shared ledger.
candidate_use_cases.human_role: Confirm decision status, assign ownership, correct language ambiguity, and approve the ledger.
candidate_use_cases.ai_role: Extract and classify candidate items from notes, link them to source passages, and flag ambiguity.

productivity.reason: Reduces manual consolidation and repeated clarification.

inclusion.reason: Bilingual normalization may improve access, but participants need a correction and non-AI path.

innovation.reason: Creates a reusable decision-memory workflow rather than a one-off summary.

tradeoffs: Adds a short approval step after each meeting
risks: AI may misclassify tentative discussion as commitment
evidence_gaps: No baseline for missed or disputed follow-ups
candidate_use_cases.non_ai_alternative: Use a structured decision-and-action template with explicit owner confirmation.

candidate_use_cases.title: Handoff acceptance assistant
candidate_use_cases.workflow_change: AI prepares a handoff packet and exception list; the receiving owner explicitly accepts, rejects, or requests clarification.
candidate_use_cases.human_role: Define completion criteria and accept responsibility for the handoff.
candidate_use_cases.ai_role: Compile context, dependencies, unresolved items, and missing acceptance fields.

impact.reason: Could prevent ownership gaps at cross-functional boundaries.

inclusion.reason: Makes expectations visible but may increase burden on receiving roles.

innovation.reason: Turns informal handoffs into an inspectable coordination mechanism.

tradeoffs: May feel bureaucratic for low-risk handoffs
risks: Teams may accept packets without reading them
evidence_gaps: Highest-risk handoff types have not been identified
candidate_use_cases.non_ai_alternative: Adopt a lightweight handoff checklist and acceptance field.

candidate_use_cases.title: Meeting portfolio and escalation review
candidate_use_cases.workflow_change: AI groups recurring unresolved decisions across meetings and prepares a weekly escalation brief for the accountable lead.
candidate_use_cases.human_role: Choose escalation thresholds and decide priorities.
candidate_use_cases.ai_role: Detect repeated unresolved items and prepare source-linked clusters.

productivity.reason: Reduces manual review across many notes.

impact.reason: May reveal systemic blockers but acts later than meeting-level confirmation.

inclusion.reason: Escalation may amplify voices that are documented more often.

innovation.reason: Creates a system-level view of decision bottlenecks.

tradeoffs: Requires consistent source records across meetings
risks: Frequency may be mistaken for importance
evidence_gaps: No agreed escalation threshold or owner capacity
candidate_use_cases.non_ai_alternative: Run a weekly unresolved-decision review using a shared register.

recommendation.why_now: It addresses the earliest failure point and can be tested without production integration.
recommendation.why_not_others_first: Handoff and portfolio views depend on first establishing trustworthy decision and action records.
recommendation.key_uncertainty: Whether human review can prevent false commitments without adding unacceptable meeting overhead.
recommendation.next_safe_action: Pilot an offline draft-and-approve ledger on six completed meetings.

mtuc.hypothesis: A source-linked AI draft plus owner approval will reduce missing or disputed actions without adding more than five minutes of review per meeting.
mtuc.scope: Six historical or low-risk meetings from two cross-functional workflows; no production writes.
human_checkpoints: Action owner accepts each assigned follow-up
mtuc.data_boundary: Use authorized meeting notes with personal details minimized; store outputs only in the approved test folder.
mtuc.baseline: Manually review the same six meetings for missing, disputed, and late follow-ups and record current review time.
success_signals: Fewer missing confirmed actions than the baseline
Every action has an accepted owner
Median human review time is five minutes or less
failure_signals: Tentative statements are repeatedly labeled as commitments
Review burden exceeds the agreed threshold
go_criteria: Improvement is observed across both workflows
revise_criteria: Errors cluster in bilingual or ambiguous notes
Review time is high but concentrated in one step
stop_criteria: A critical decision is falsely recorded after review
Participants lose access to a non-AI correction path
Data handling violates the approved boundary
mtuc.review_point: After six meetings and before any live-system integration

required_controls: No production write during the test

ai_inferred: The first leverage point is confirmation before handoff

next_decision: Confirm whether six low-risk meetings and a five-minute review threshold are acceptable for the first test.
